transcript.content: Hello, what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... I just haven't been able to shake this feeling. Ever since my friend was killed, I've just been living with this constant mix of guilt, fear, and anger. People kept telling me it would get better with time, that it would ease up, but... it really hasn't. It's just always there.
Do you find yourself persistently yearning or longing for your friend?

No, not really. I mean, I miss her, of course, but it's not this constant yearning or longing. It's more about the... the circumstances of how she died, and how it left me feeling. The anger and the guilt are what really stick with me, not so much a deep longing for her.
Do unwanted memories of your friend’s death keep coming into your mind, even when you don’t want them to?

Yes, they do. It doesn't even take much to trigger it, honestly. Um, a crosswalk signal, or hearing the growl of a truck driving by... even just seeing a walking-tour map. Any of those things can suddenly put the whole scene right back in my head. It comes back so sharply. It's like... I can actually see my friend stepping off the curb all over again, and I just can't stop the memory from playing out in my mind.
Were you present and did you witness your friend being killed as it happened?
Yes, I was. We were just... walking together. I was right there and saw the whole thing happen.
How long ago did your friend’s death happen?
It was about two years and three months ago. That's when she was killed on that walking tour, and... well, all of this has been going on ever since.
Do you deliberately avoid places, activities, conversations, or other reminders that bring back the memory of your friend’s death?

Yes, I do. I actually go out of my way to avoid that intersection completely now. And... well, I've stopped signing up for most tours, or even local safety meetings. I just can't bear it when the conversations circle back to what happened there, so I'd rather just stay away from all of it.
Since your friend’s death, have you often felt unusually watchful or on guard, as if danger could happen at any moment?

Yes, I do. Especially if I'm anywhere near traffic. I just... I find myself watching every single truck, the curbs, every pedestrian around me. It feels like it's my responsibility to catch the danger before it happens again.
Since your friend’s death, have you had trouble sleeping?
No, not really. My sleep has been mostly fine. I mean, I sleep about as well as I always have, so I haven't noticed any real trouble with that since it happened.
Since your friend’s death, have you found yourself startling much more easily than you did before?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm definitely more watchful, like I said before, but I don't really jump at sudden noises or anything like that. I haven't noticed being any more easily startled than I used to be.
Since your friend’s death, have you had difficulty concentrating?

Yes, I have. It's been quite noticeable, actually. When I try to balance the budget for the senior center or even just read through a program schedule, the numbers and dates just sort of blur together. I find myself having to check the same simple thing over and over again because my mind just won't hold onto it. It's like I can't keep my focus on what's right in front of me.
